COPT.name: All-Round Overachiever
COPT.portrait: The complete research machine: gets work done, leads others, withstands pressure and takes responsibility. Can carry an entire research strand alone.
pros: Broad capabilities; can carry a research strand alone
Responsible, resilient and proactive with solutions
Unreasonably dependable when it matters
cons: Prone to overwork and running on fumes
Takes everything on, leaving teammates little room to develop
Doing everything personally can make them a bottleneck
COPT.mentorStrategy: A rare creature. Protect against burnout and the team becoming dependent on their doing everything. Give substantial autonomy and explicit appreciation.
mentorActions: Give autonomy and clear recognition
Help them delegate and set boundaries instead of carrying everything
Watch workload to prevent burnout
Turn their methods into team procedures rather than endless personal rescue
mentorTips: Offer substantial autonomy and explicit appreciation
Set workload limits and insist on rest before they burn out
Leave room for others to take ownership and develop

COPW.name: Paper-Tiger Achiever
COPW.tagline: A champion on weekdays, a rookie at crunch time
COPW.portrait: Works hard and plans beautifully day to day, but may retreat under the pressure of a major defense or revision and hesitate to make decisions.
pros: Hardworking, well organized and effective in daily execution
A dependable mainstay in their regular role
cons: May unravel at high-stakes defenses or major revisions
Hesitates to decide and retreats from crucial choices
COPW.mentorStrategy: Useful, but not ready to carry everything alone. A supervisor should provide support at critical moments and avoid leaving high-pressure decisions entirely to them.
mentorActions: Stay involved at critical points rather than leaving decisions to them alone
Provide reassurance and make your support explicit
Rehearse defenses and other stressful events in advance
Break major decisions into smaller ones to reduce concentrated pressure
mentorTips: Be present at critical moments and provide emotional support
Rehearse stressful situations and prepare mentally
Pair them with someone who can help make major decisions

CORT.name: Silent Workhorse
CORT.tagline: Finishes the work, remembers to report three days later
CORT.portrait: Quietly gets the work done and holds up when trouble hits, but routine communication is seriously delayed.
pros: Steady, hardworking and consistently productive
Stays when problems arise rather than walking away
cons: Updates arrive extremely late, sometimes days after completion
Can work in the wrong direction for a long time before anyone notices
CORT.mentorStrategy: Require regular written or meeting updates and firm milestones, so they do not quietly pursue the wrong direction until it is too late.
mentorActions: Require weekly or group-meeting progress reports
Set firm milestones and regularly align direction
Ask for progress rather than waiting for an update
Recognize their output publicly so it is visible
mentorTips: Require regular updates and firm milestones
Actively check progress instead of waiting for reports
Make timely disclosure of problems part of the expectations

CORW.name: Overthinking Cabbage
CORW.tagline: Does the most work, spends the longest worrying
CORW.portrait: Does a great deal but hesitates to speak, submits at the last minute and withdraws in a crisis. Much energy goes into inner conflict.
pros: Productive, demanding of themselves and willing to dig deep
Their work is often good quality
cons: Heavy inner conflict despite doing a lot of work
Hesitates to communicate, submits late and avoids crises
CORW.mentorStrategy: A productive but emotionally vulnerable worker. Offer gentle guidance and actively check progress. Harsh public criticism can make them withdraw or give up.
mentorActions: Guide gently and check progress regularly
Avoid harsh public criticism that may trigger withdrawal
Break tasks down and reduce perfectionist pressure
Create a safe way to ask for help
mentorTips: Gently ask for progress instead of waiting for submission
Avoid harsh public criticism that can make them give up
Break large goals into smaller steps to ease the mental load

CAPT.name: Rational Partner
CAPT.tagline: Excellent within scope. Extras sold separately.
CAPT.portrait: The ideal professional: clear responsibilities, early warnings and resilience when things go wrong, but no work beyond the agreed scope.
pros: Clear about responsibilities, flags risks early and holds up under pressure
Dependable within boundaries; a strong professional teammate
cons: Refuses out-of-scope work and may seem rather distant
Reluctant to carry additional responsibilities for the team
CAPT.mentorStrategy: Well suited to project management. Use clear agreements and reward contributions; do not pressure them with appeals to selfless dedication.
mentorActions: Use explicit agreements, roles and contribution-based rewards
Avoid guilt-based appeals to sacrifice
Consider assigning project management responsibilities
Clarify authority, responsibilities and expected returns
mentorTips: A good project-manager fit with explicit agreements and roles
Reward contributions instead of invoking self-sacrifice
Agree authority, responsibilities and rewards upfront for steady delivery

CAPW.name: Self-Preserving Executive
CAPW.tagline: When trouble takes flight, I'm already airborne
CAPW.portrait: Excellent at their own job and proactive in communication, but stays within scope and protects themselves first when major trouble arrives.
pros: Excellent in their own role, communicative and efficient
cons: Works within scope and puts self-preservation first in a crisis
Unreliable as the final safety net; may leave when things get difficult
CAPW.mentorStrategy: Capable, but not someone to rely on for personal loyalty. Set clear boundaries and incentives rather than appealing to dedication.
mentorActions: Use their skills without assuming personal loyalty
Define roles clearly and use concrete incentives
Have a separate backup rather than relying on them to rescue a crisis
Put responsibilities in writing
mentorTips: A capable worker, but do not assume personal loyalty
Use clear roles and incentives rather than appeals to dedication
Keep a backup for tasks that require someone to carry the final risk

CART.name: Quiet Tech Wizard
CART.tagline: Skip the small talk. Show me the bug.
CART.portrait: Focuses on their own patch and does not seek extra problems, but has strong technical skills and can withstand trouble.
pros: Technically strong, resilient, focused and self-driven
cons: Does not seek extra work; weak coordination and reactive communication
CART.mentorStrategy: Assign focused technical challenges and minimize interpersonal coordination duties.
mentorActions: Give technical problem-solving work and fewer coordination tasks
Use documents and asynchronous communication instead of forcing meeting speeches
Set clear technical goals and avoid micromanaging the process
mentorTips: Use for focused technical challenges with less coordination work
Prefer written or asynchronous communication over frequent meetings
Set clear technical goals, then give them room to solve the problem

CARW.name: Lab Invisible
CARW.tagline: No trace found. Definitely still here.
CARW.portrait: Does the bare minimum, neither initiates nor clearly refuses, avoids responsibility and shrinks away when trouble comes.
pros: Can complete basic independent work without causing much disturbance
cons: Neither initiates, refuses nor takes responsibility; withdraws in trouble
Low visibility and contribution; almost impossible to find
CARW.mentorStrategy: Keep them away from central responsibilities. Assign low-risk, independent support work.
mentorActions: Use low-risk, independent supporting work rather than central roles
Set explicit checklists and acceptance points to ensure delivery
Keep them off the critical path
mentorTips: Assign low-risk, independent support tasks
Use small, explicit assignments and firm deadlines
Check in by name regularly so they do not disappear entirely

XOPT.name: Scapegoat Fire Chief
XOPT.tagline: Does the heavy lifting, gets the hardest debrief
XOPT.portrait: Works extremely hard and steps up in trouble, but usually blames the environment and may end up doing thankless heavy lifting.
pros: Works hard, steps up in trouble and proactively fills gaps
A major source of effort and emergency support
cons: Usually attributes mistakes to the environment
May do thankless work and blame external factors during reviews
XOPT.mentorStrategy: Recognize their effort while firmly challenging their explanations during reviews. Help them build a useful way to learn from setbacks.
mentorActions: Acknowledge their effort and provide positive feedback
Challenge external blame in reviews and start with personal improvements
Separate controllable from uncontrollable factors to reduce wasted effort
mentorTips: Recognize the effort first and help them settle emotionally
Insist on a list of things they personally can improve during reviews
Watch for burnout from long-standing feelings of unfairness

XOPW.name: Overcommitting Big Kid
XOPW.tagline: First to take the blame, first to pass it on
XOPW.portrait: Volunteers for everything, then blames everyone else when it goes wrong and avoids the decisive moment.
pros: Eager to take work and participate; appears highly enthusiastic
cons: When work fails, it is always someone else's fault
Avoids critical moments and leaves a mess after overstepping boundaries
XOPW.mentorStrategy: A high-risk pattern. Enforce firm boundaries on overstepping and require meaningful accountability for mistakes.
mentorActions: High risk: strictly limit work beyond agreed responsibilities
Require real accountability and prevent blame shifting
Keep written records of responsibilities
Avoid core assignments
mentorTips: High risk: enforce clear limits on taking over others' work
Require real accountability for mistakes rather than rescuing everything
Keep written records throughout to prevent blame shifting afterward

XORT.name: Grumbling Scapegoat
XORT.tagline: Everyone is against me. I'll carry it anyway.
XORT.portrait: Does the most work, says little day to day and pushes through crises, but carries many complaints and feels the world is against them.
pros: Works extensively and remains present when things get difficult
cons: Full of complaints and feels singled out by everyone
Rarely communicates proactively and spends much emotional energy
XORT.mentorStrategy: Stand up for them, remove some excess responsibility and teach them to communicate needs upward.
mentorActions: Back them up and remove some excess responsibilities
Teach them to communicate needs and manage upward
Challenge unhelpful attribution during reviews
Provide an outlet before resentment erupts
mentorTips: Stand up for them and relieve excess responsibility
Help them communicate needs to supervisors
Check in emotionally and make their contributions visible

XORW.name: Quantum Blame Shifter
XORW.tagline: Schrödinger's teammate: working until observed, then blaming
XORW.portrait: Seems highly involved but produces little. Retreats when trouble hits, explains everything through external causes afterward, and still expects others to pick up the pieces.
pros: Appears highly involved and packages their presence convincingly
cons: Almost no substantive output
Retreats in a crisis and blames external causes afterward
Still confidently expects others to cover for them
XORW.mentorStrategy: Keep away from core roles. Remove the expectation of rescue and manage with firm deadlines and concrete deliverables.
mentorActions: High risk: avoid core roles
Use firm deadlines and concrete deliverables without an automatic safety net
Move deadlines earlier to reduce hidden delays
Require written records and a clear crisis intervention procedure
Limit assignments to independent supporting work
mentorTips: Avoid core roles
Use firm deadlines and deliverables without an automatic rescue expectation
Set earlier delivery checkpoints and document progress throughout

XAPT.name: Confident Average
XAPT.portrait: Produces ordinary work and avoids extras, but withstands pressure exceptionally well, shifts blame confidently and keeps bouncing back.
pros: Exceptionally resilient, steady and hard to discourage
Willing to communicate and unfazed by an audience
cons: Ordinary output with little initiative for extra work
Confident blame shifting and inflated self-evaluation
XAPT.mentorStrategy: Hard to change. Use firm, measurable performance expectations instead of relying on explanations alone.
mentorActions: Use concrete performance measures and judge results rather than explanations
Rely on systems rather than persuasion
Use roles requiring resilience without demanding exceptionally high output
mentorTips: Use firm, measurable targets and look at results rather than explanations
Define and enforce minimum output standards
Do not let confident talk distract from actual progress

XAPW.name: Smooth-Talking Slacker
XAPW.tagline: Proactive with excuses. Reactive with work.
XAPW.portrait: Quick to offer excuses, leaves when trouble appears and passes the work to everyone else.
pros: Verbally proactive, socially agile and apparently active
cons: Proactively finds excuses, runs from trouble and passes work to others
XAPW.mentorStrategy: Consider ending the collaboration or reducing their role.
mentorActions: High risk: consider ending collaboration or reducing their role
Do not assign critical tasks
Use concrete deliverables and written records
mentorTips: Consider ending the collaboration or reducing their role first
If retained, use independent small tasks off the critical path with written records
Watch the effect on team working habits

XART.name: Unbudgeable Wall
XART.tagline: Takes the criticism. Keeps the habits.
XART.portrait: Does little work and communicates little, but is emotionally unshakable. Takes criticism without answering back, then changes nothing.
pros: Emotionally steady and rarely reacts to criticism
cons: Does little work, communicates little and changes nothing
Very resistant to influence and costly to manage
XART.mentorStrategy: Stop trying to remake them. Maintain minimum standards and keep the team from being dragged down.
mentorActions: Focus on minimum standards rather than changing the person
Use basic, firm delivery requirements
Avoid disproportionate management effort
mentorTips: Focus on minimum standards so the team is not held back
Apply the agreed process if minimum deliverables are not met
Reduce emotional investment and deal with specific work through clear procedures

XARW.name: Lab Time Bomb
XARW.portrait: Failure across the board: does not work, hides when trouble hits and blames the environment.
pros: Frankly, strengths are hard to find. At least the disengagement is visible rather than disguised as busyness.
cons: Does not work, avoids trouble and blames everything on the environment
mentorActions: High risk: end the collaboration decisively
Keep them away from critical dependencies during the transition
mentorTips: End the collaboration decisively
Keep written records and arrange a careful handover before separation
Do not assign work that others depend on
